final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful insofar as it concedes the key gaps: the affected use case is still exposed, the risk acceptance draft is unapproved and incomplete, and the record does not establish that disclosure alone satisfies policy. Those concessions make the position less overbroad, but they do not cure the unresolved compliance predicate identified in the initial report. Under the provided policy text, rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring do not by themselves make launch supportable when the affected segment remains exposed; exclusion of the use case or reviewed risk acceptance is still required for mitigation to count in the relevant way. Because the record does not confirm launch without disclosure and does not conclusively show a false certification statement, escalation to noncompliant is not yet justified. But the missing approval link remains unresolved, so compliant or compliant_with_caveats is not supported.
remaining_concerns: The emergency shelter placement use case remains exposed in the launch cohort on the current record.
There is no reviewed or approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed emergency shelter placement segment.
The policy text says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate this weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable.
No admissible evidence shows that disclosure alone satisfies the policy predicate for an exposed named use case.
The recommendation to certify remains unsupported on the present evidentiary record.
